legal-regulatory.summary: Re-verification confirms the core documented claims held up well: the BBB F-rating profile, the NY AG consumer alert quotes, the CourtListener/Spillemyndigheden access failures, and Action Network's lawsuit-tracker state-by-state facts (Nevada injunction, AZ criminal charges, Third Circuit ruling, CFTC-vs-states suit, CFTC chair quote) all reproduced exactly on independent re-fetch. However, verification surfaced two real errors in the draft that have been corrected: (1) a fabricated or unsupported dollar figure - the draft claimed Brazil regulation would cost Better Collective EUR 20-30M in 2025, but that does not match any source found; multiple outlets (Gambling Insider, esportsinsider, SBC News) instead report a EUR 7m negative Q1 2025 vs Q1 2024 revenue and EBITDA impact, a materially smaller and differently-scoped figure; and (2) a state mix-up - the draft attributed a 200 dollar application fee to Virginia's flat-fee-affiliate vendor registration, but Virginia's actual fee is 500 dollars; the 200 dollar figure belongs to Michigan's equivalent registration. One characterization was also softened: Action Network's article does not use the word unprecedented to describe the CFTC's suit against Arizona, Connecticut and Illinois (it says this was the first time the federal government sued states over this), so that specific phrasing has been corrected, while the CFTC chair's nullify-federal-law quote was verified verbatim. The bottom-line finding, that no lawsuits, FTC actions, or state AG enforcement actions were found naming Action Network or Better Collective specifically, remains a clean, well-searched nothing-found result, still appropriately caveated as index-search-based rather than a direct docket or PACER pull.

Two real problems found: (1) the draft's speculative gloss on the "approaching 40 million" stat ("likely monthly page views/impressions") is very likely wrong — a separate, independently-located primary source (Better Collective's May 3, 2021 deal-announcement press release) uses the near-identical phrase "approaching 40 mUSD" to describe Action Network's projected 2021 REVENUE, strongly suggesting the deck's unlabeled figure is a revenue run-rate, not a traffic metric; this also means the draft's uncited "$40M run-rate" sub-claim, previously unsourced, is now confirmed and properly sourced. (2) The LeadIQ "$35M revenue" figure could not be reproduced — re-fetching the exact same URL now returns a "$10M–$25M" range, contradicting the draft's number; this should be treated as unreliable regardless. Also found and corrected a minor address error (registered address is "Sankt Annæ Plads 26-28, 1250 Copenhagen K" not "...Plads 28...København K") and enriched the deal-structure finding with details the draft omitted (a $10M deferred-cash tranche and exact 412,923-share/6-24-month-lockup mechanics), sourced from Better Collective's own closing-announcement press release. The central "no standalone Action Network financials disclosed" finding — the load-bearing claim of the whole research angle — holds up fully on re-verification.

Completion expected in Q2 2021', 'Governance / Management | Action to operate as a separate business unit led by Action President and CEO Patrick Keane.' Independently confirmed via Better Collective's own May 28, 2021 closing announcement (GlobeNewswire) and the May 3, 2021 signing announcement, which add mechanics the draft omitted: purchase price '240 mUSD (198 mEUR)' was cash plus 'a 11.4 mUSD issuance of new Better Collective (BETCO.ST) shares'; '412,923 shares' issued at '231.35 SEK' (~$27.61), a 5-trading-day weighted average before the May 3, 2021 signing, subject to '6 and 24 months' lock-up, subscribed for by 'Action's management and certain key employees'; additionally '10 mUSD of the cash payment' was 'paid on a deferred basis' to settle 'existing share options in Action.' No performance-based earnout/contingent-consideration language was found in either the deck or the closing announcement — the draft's 'no earnout found' conclusion holds, though it should be described as 'no earnout found in the deal-closing documents reviewed' rather than a full negative proof, since 2021-2023 annual report purchase-price-allocation notes were not separately checked.

expert-pick-accuracy.summary: Action Network has NO public accuracy-grading methodology for its human "Experts" (pundits/writers) comparable to FantasyPros' Accuracy Challenge. What it has instead is (a) a documented A-F statistical grading formula (ROI Z-score + overfitting penalty) but that applies only to algorithmic "PRO Systems," never to human experts; and (b) raw, transparent, ungraded track-record tables per expert (record/win%/units, broken out by Yesterday/7d/30d/All-Time and by sport) plus a rules-based "verified bet" anti-gaming standard (locks to consensus lines, immutable, 0.5-3u, no live/futures/heavy-favorite bets, no doubling a side). Discovery of experts is unit/ROI-sorted by default (not win%-sorted), and is split across three separate non-merged lists (Verified Experts / Hot Streak Bettors / Popular Bettors) rather than one accuracy-weighted consensus — i.e., no FantasyPros-style accuracy-weighted filtering lever exists on the public surface.

Most systems grade 'A'.
findings.evidence: Direct quote from the article: 'The grade is a report card that tells you the strength of the system based on two major factors: 1. ROI Score (ZScore)... 2. Overfitting Score (Too many selected items/filters)...'

findings.point: A documented 'verified bet' rule-set functions as an anti-gaming standard, not an accuracy methodology

findings.point: NJ Division of Gaming Enforcement (DGE) cease action, Feb 2019, for promoting offshore/unlicensed sportsbooks

business-model.summary: All four sites monetize sports content, but via three distinct patterns. Covers.com and OddsShark are affiliate-first: free forum/editorial/picks content wrapped in extensive sportsbook promo-code navigation, with no paywalls found. VegasInsider is a hybrid — the same affiliate machinery PLUS a genuine direct-subscription tier (VI Premium). WagerTalk is the outlier: a pure direct-sale marketplace (per-pick, Flex Picks, Power Pass) with no sportsbook affiliate links found anywhere on its customer-facing pages. On the two explicitly-flagged resolution threads, both check out under re-verification: VegasInsider's Action Network connection is fully resolved — both are Better Collective brands (Better Collective USA, Inc. operates VegasInsider per its own terms-of-use page; Better Collective's own GlobeNewswire release confirms it closed the $240M cash-plus-$11.4M-stock acquisition of Action Network, Inc. on May 28, 2021), which explains the shared widgets/CDN and rules out the competing "GDC Group" (Gambling.com Group) lead for VegasInsider specifically. legal-regulatory.summary: No lawsuits, litigation, or legal disputes involving SportsData.io (SportsDataIO / FantasyData LLC) were found across CourtListener, PACERMonitor, Justia Dockets, and general web search — a clean record as far as public-source OSINT can establish. SportsData.io holds no "official data" designation from the NFL, MLB, NBA, or NHL; it operates as a non-exclusive aggregator/reseller competing against Sportradar and Genius Sports, who do hold those official league rights. This distinction carries real legal weight because Tennessee, Illinois, and Michigan passed statutes (2019) requiring licensed sportsbooks to use "official league data" for certain bet types (live/in-play and some props) — placing SportsData.io's product outside the mandated category for that narrow slice of wagering in those states. A significant disambiguation risk was found and resolved: a same-named but distinct company, "SportsData LLC" of St. Paul, MN (founded 2010 by Rob Phythian and Dave Abbott), was acquired by Sportradar in December 2013 and renamed Sportradar US — this is NOT SportsData.io/FantasyData LLC (Philadelphia-based, founded 2008 by Scott Gimpel), and a Wikipedia entry appears to misdate this same 2013 event as "December 2023," which would otherwise create a false impression that SportsData.io itself was absorbed by a rival.

findings.point: The 'official league data' legal mandate creates a documented regulatory boundary that structurally excludes non-official vendors like SportsData.io from part of the regulated market
findings.detail: Tennessee (HB1, effective July 1, 2019) was the first state to require licensed operators to 'exclusively use official league data for purposes of live betting.' Illinois followed in 2019, mandating official league data specifically for proposition/prop bets. Michigan passed a similar requirement conditioned on the data being offered 'on commercially reasonable terms.' Because SportsData.io is not an official league designee, its odds/stats feeds would not satisfy these specific statutory carve-outs in those three states for the bet types covered — though this doesn't bar SportsData.io from all other uses (fantasy, non-live pre-match odds, news/stats, media) in those or other states.

findings.point: Corporate lineage is a clean, non-litigated series of internal restructurings, not contentious M&A
findings.detail: Originally FantasyData LLC (founded 2008 by Scott Gimpel). In April 2019, FantasyData split: the commercial/B2B API division rebranded as SportsDataIO, while the consumer-facing FantasyData.com and BettingData.com brands remained. In February 2022, SportsDataIO spun the consumer brands (FantasyData.com, BettingData.com) into a new entity, Left Brain Sports LLC, which simultaneously acquired FantasyFootballCalculator.com and PicksCalculator.com, with FFC's prior owner Kevin Day installed as Left Brain Sports' CEO. No dispute, breach, or litigation was found connected to any of these transitions; the 2019 press release describes both post-split companies as 'privately held and debt-free.'
findings.evidence: prnewswire.com 'FantasyData Rebrands Commercial API Division to SportsDataIO and Announces New Consumer APIs' (2019); prnewswire.com 'SportsDataIO Launches Left Brain Sports; Acquires Betting & Fantasy Brands' (Feb 8, 2022); smartbusinessdealmakers.com corroborating the Left Brain Sports transaction.

api-data-model-teardown.summary: Pulled SportsData.io's public NFL developer docs (Coverage, API Documentation, Data Dictionary, Fantasy Scoring System) plus five product pages (Live Odds API, Fantasy Sports API, SDX ID Mapping, Replay, Global API). Confirmed a fully public, no-login developer portal with concrete REST endpoint URLs, field-level schemas, and a named proprietary prediction engine (\"BAKER\") used for both betting picks and fantasy projections. Also surfaced named enterprise customers beyond Fanatics (Xfinity, Entain, FanDuel, Microsoft, Ubisoft, Underdog) on the Global API marketing page, and a second data-provider relationship (RotoBaller, for player news).

findings.point: REST API base URL, versioning and auth scheme are fully documented publicly
findings.detail: Base pattern: https://api.sportsdata.io/v3/nfl/{namespace}/json/{Endpoint}/{params}. Namespaces observed: scores (Standings, Teams, Players, Stadiums), stats (ScoresFinal, BoxScoreFinal, PlayerGameStatsBySeason, PlayerGameRedZoneStats), odds (BettingMetadata, ActiveSportsbooks, GameOdds), projections (InjuredPlayers, IdpPlayerGameProjectionStatsByWeek, FantasyDefenseProjectionsBySeason). Auth is via API key passed either as a query parameter or via HTTP header `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: {key}` — the header name is the Azure API Management (APIM) default, indicating SportsData.io fronts its API with Azure APIM as the gateway/key-management layer. Responses available as JSON or XML.
findings.evidence: sportsdata.io/developers/api-documentation/nfl — literal endpoint URLs (e.g. https://api.sportsdata.io/v3/nfl/scores/json/Standings/{season}, https://api.sportsdata.io/v3/nfl/odds/json/BettingMetadata, https://api.sportsdata.io/v3/nfl/projections/json/FantasyDefenseProjectionsBySeason/{season}) and the literal text 'The API key can be passed either as a query parameter or using the following HTTP request header. `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: {key}`'

findings.point: SportsData.io runs a proprietary predictive/simulation engine called BAKER, used for both sportsbook trading/pricing and fantasy projections
findings.detail: BAKER is described as capable of answering 'practically any question about a future event or outcome,' producing a 'Best Bets' feed with true pricing, EV and ROI against live market prices, and offering a 'Query API to build your own question sets.' Critically, the copy states BAKER 'Simulates every game of the season 10,000 times' and 'All simulations correlated' — i.e. a Monte Carlo game-simulation engine, not just a regression/ML point-estimate model. On the fantasy side, BAKER (not just 'Legacy') generates fantasy projections across all skill positions/scoring categories for daily/weekly, season-long, partial-season/rest-of-season, and even 'dynasty careers,' plus floor/ceiling and head-to-head matchup outputs. The dedicated URL sportsdata.io/baker-predictive-engine 404s ('Oops! We can't seem to find the page') as of this pull, so the engine's own detail page is currently broken/removed even though it's linked from two live product pages.
findings.evidence: sportsdata.io/live-odds-api: 'our BAKER Engine can be leveraged as a primary or cross-check pricing engine...Our BAKER Engine can answer practically any question...Simulates every game of the season 10,000 times / All simulations correlated'; sportsdata.io/fantasy-sports-api: 'Our BAKER Engine provides fantasy projections across all skill positions and scoring categories for daily/weekly, season-long, partial seasons & rest of season, and dynasty careers. Leverage its power to further produce floor/ceiling, head to head matchups'; sportsdata.io/developers/coverages/nfl: 'SportsDataIO Supports 2 different projection models (BAKER and Legacy)'; sportsdata.io/baker-predictive-engine returned a 404 page

findings.point: NFL fantasy scoring methodology is fully published as an exact rule table (a genuine, citable methodology document)
findings.detail: Default SportsDataIO scoring: Passing 1pt/25yds, 4pt TD, -2 INT; Rushing 1pt/10yds, 6pt TD; Receiving 1pt/10yds, 6pt TD, reception=1pt only if PPR; 2pt conversions=2; fumble lost=-2; fumble return TD=6. Team D/ST: sack=1, INT=2, fumble rec=2, safety=2, def/return TD=6, 2pt return=2, points-allowed tiers from +10 (shutout) down to -4 (35+ allowed). IDP: solo tackle=1, assist=0.5, sack=2 (plus 1pt/10 sack yards separately), TFL=1, QB hit=1, pass defended=1, INT=3, forced/recovered fumble=3, def TD=6. Kicking: PAT=1, FG 0-49=3, FG 50+=5 (no separate short-FG tier below 50, unlike some competitors' more granular kicking tables).
findings.evidence: sportsdata.io/developers/fantasy-scoring-system/nfl — full itemized point table under headers Overview / Offensive Players / Team Defense-Special Teams / Individual Defensive Players / Kicking

findings.point: Data Dictionary exposes granular, versioned (dated) field-level schemas per object, including provenance/scrambling flags
findings.detail: Example: PlayerGameProjection object (in production since 2013) has ~70 fields spanning passing/rushing/receiving/return/defensive/kicking stat projections plus FantasyPoints and FantasyPointsPPR, each tagged with Name/Type/Size/Nullable/Scrambled/CSV columns. The 'Scrambled' column indicates certain fields (nearly all numeric stat fields) are obfuscated on lower/trial tiers -- a concrete technical detail about how their free-trial data is intentionally degraded. GameOdd object (since 2018) includes HomeMoneyLine/AwayMoneyLine/DrawMoneyLine, Home/AwayPointSpread + payouts, OverUnder + Over/UnderPayout, SportsbookId, OddType (live/pregame/1st-half/1st-qtr), and an 'Unlisted' timestamp field marking when a line was pulled from the book. GameOddResult and GameOddOutcome objects (since 2024, newer) add BetValue vs ActualValue and a GameOddResultType enum (Won/Lost/Push/Not Resulted/Incomplete) for graded/resulted bets.
findings.evidence: sportsdata.io/developers/data-dictionary/nfl — full column tables for PlayerGameProjection, GameOdd, GameOddOutcome, GameOddResult, each with a '(From {year})' provenance tag

findings.point: Coverage doc confirms two distinct betting-odds delivery tiers and a resulting/grading add-on, implying a tiered commercial product structure
findings.detail: Game Lines split into 'Pre-Game Lines' (base) vs 'Pre-Game Lines Plus' (adds full line-movement history) and 'In-Play Lines' vs 'In-Play Lines Plus' (same distinction live). Plus-tier and 'Sportsbook Group' endpoints appear to be higher/enterprise tiers gated behind a required URL parameter. 'Resulting' (whether a bet would have won/lost/pushed) is explicitly called out as available 'as an add-on' rather than included by default. Odds sourced from '20+ sportsbooks' with an aggregated 'SportsDataIO Consensus Line.' Props/Futures follow the same pre-match-only, no-resulting-by-default pattern.
findings.evidence: sportsdata.io/developers/coverages/nfl — headers '#### Pre-Game Lines' vs '#### Pre-Game Lines Plus' vs '#### In-Play Lines' vs '#### In-Play Lines Plus'; text 'Does not include resulting of game line markets' (base tiers) vs 'Includes all line movement for pre game odds markets...See our Aggregated Odds resulting guide' (Plus tiers); 'Odds markets are available from 20+ sports books including a consensus line'

findings.point: Global API is a genuinely separate product line from the flagship 'League API,' with a unified cross-sport schema, and lists named enterprise customers not previously confirmed

patents-ip.summary: Clean "nothing found" across every reasonable entity/inventor variant: SportsData.io / FantasyData LLC (its actual legal entity name) holds zero patents in Google Patents (which aggregates USPTO+WIPO+EPO+dozens of national offices) and zero in Justia's independent USPTO index.
